vocab.top_half: wave 2 (this key name is historical): cohorts 1 and 2 of the maintainers' frozen membership file; as adopted of 5 Sep it is plotted because generation finished there first, wave 1+2 before wave 2 on its own; a plotted set (dataset switch value top), not a change of the frame or of the fits (rule of 3 Sep: fit on all data; tiers are membership labels)
vocab.board_plus_top_half: wave 1+2 (this key name is historical): wave 1, the kept tasks of the original set, together with wave 2 on one axis, the first plotted set of 5 Sep (dataset switch value board_top); wave 2 parked (the former cohorts 3 and 4) is excluded from this plot and from wave 2 by itself, never from the frame; wave 1 is already mostly fitted and offers less variety
vocab.task_tier: a task's tier is its the maintainers cohort (the difficulty level sets of 3 Sep), the cohort column (1 to 4) of the maintainers' frozen membership file of 4 Sep; the first two tiers, uniform in difficulty, are cohorts 1 and 2 = wave 2 (877 tasks at the freeze); cohorts 3 and 4 are wave 2 parked (897 at the freeze); three tier words stay apart: task tier = cohort, model tier = the order-of-filling's model tiers (the first model tier = the golden set), judge tier = judge_tier; a tier is a membership label and never a filter on results (the 3 Sep rule: fit on all data)
vocab.house_bandwidth: the reference local-logistic kernel's bandwidth is a fixed width of one unit on the difficulty scale (adopted 4 Sep), never a fraction of the axis span or of the extremes; curves stay comparable across the dataset switch; the adaptive options (per-model CV, ESS-targeted) stay under evaluation against this baseline with the three sign-off criteria
vocab.axis_smoothing: the difficulty axis is the model-average failure rate placed on the difficulty scale (fail rate stretched at both ends), models equal-weighted, with ONE Jeffreys pseudo-observation per task on its total attempts: q_t = (N_t p̄_t + ½)/(N_t + 1) (equal n: (Σf+½)/(Σn+1)); never one ½ per model before averaging (that shrinks toward ½ by n/(n+1) and confines a one-attempt axis to a narrow band around the middle (no task can read easier than about one in four failing or harder than about three in four)); a count-based axis resolves positions only within about ±log(2N_t+1), beyond which and under few attempts the joint fit places tasks; served waves keep their cut-time axis until the big fit's cut switches the recipe (adopted 4 Sep on experiment-design's measurement)
vocab.curve_of_record: both reserved words are read off the average-rate curve: the expected failure rate over the tasks at a difficulty with the fitted task spread included (capability = its 50% crossing, reliability = its 1% crossing); the median-task crossing is the labelled second option, never under the bare word; the maintainers' crossings_of_record carries the average-rate reading as d1_of_record (export switched in the first week of September; d1_median_task_z beside it); a table that reads D99 from the typical (median-task) curve says so under a flag (adopted 4 Sep; direction of 3 Sep: the 1% crossing is the reliability readout, the Bayesian fit is preferred for averages, the median-task reading is an alternative)
vocab.curve_of_record_updated: updated 9 Sep: the clause about the maintainers' pending export switch retired; axis_smoothing and every other key unchanged
vocab.qualified_use: 10 Sep: the bare reserved words name the failure curve's crossings only; a crossing of any other curve carries a qualifier at first use and never the bare word (e.g. 'alignment reliability' = the difficulty at which a misbehaviour rate crosses 1%, testbed-feasibility, 10 Sep); readouts of any crossing are the difficulty percent, never a count of tasks below or above (adopted 10 Sep)

enforced.golden set: the 12 models of Definitions' golden set list (Qwen3 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B each plain and thinking; Claude Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 each plain and thinking), derived from the registry field golden_set=true; forms: golden set, golden model(s), golden(-set) axis, golden fit(s), golden curve(s); on counts 'golden set (12)' counts models; every golden number carries the note 'a data point, not the difficulty definition' (adopted 3 Sep); not used: 'golden models' as a count noun, 'golden population', 'derisking set', 'golden frame' (adopted 3 Sep)
enforced.average-rate 1% crossing: where the model's fitted average failure rate first reaches 1%
enforced.median-task 1% crossing: where the median task's failure rate reaches 1%
enforced.average-rate 50% crossing: where the fitted average failure rate reaches even odds
enforced.median-task 50% crossing: where the median task reaches even odds
enforced.level pair (1%, 50%): two linked crossings of one trend, always written with concrete levels — never variables
enforced.cumulative 1% failure rate: the hardest difficulty such that average failure over ALL easier tasks is still ≤ 1%
enforced.worst-stretch 1% failure rate: the same, but EVERY trailing stretch of easier tasks must stay ≤ 1% — easy wins cannot bank budget for later failures
enforced.first task above 1% failure: the last difficulty before the first single task failing more than 1%
enforced.cumulative X% failure rate: the same machine at any other concrete anchor
enforced.99%-assured: prefix: quoted at the value it holds with 99% posterior probability

soft.success-mass balance point: everything the model solves, added up and read as one position on the difficulty axis — mean pass rate expressed as a difficulty
soft.contested mass: how much of the difficulty axis the model SOMETIMES solves and sometimes fails — the width of its struggle zone
soft.easy-success subsidy: cumulative minus worst-stretch: how much quoted range was earned by easy wins rather than held everywhere

dropped_no_unification: the counting nouns for models and their settings
frontier reads (dark range, d2, dM, solved-mass edge, L)

scope.binds: value labels — wherever a bare reserved word functions as the label of a displayed number (axis names, tooltip labels, table headers over numbers, stat-tile captions)
scope.exempt_tool_names: tool/site/page names denote subject matter, not measurements, and are exempt
scope.litmus: if deleting the word would leave a number unlabeled, the reservation applies; if it would merely rename a surface, it does not
scope.gloss_pattern: a bare reserved word may gloss its own adopted metric when the full adopted name is adjacent (e.g. 'Capability: average-rate 50% crossing', average chain at adopted levels only — the CROSSINGS pattern, blessed)

crossings_plots_axis_names.D50: the average-rate 50% crossing (the capability crossing): its name wherever the crossing is named by symbol
crossings_plots_axis_names.D99: the average-rate 1% crossing (the reliability crossing), named by the success side: 99% of answers pass where 1% fail; the same quantity as the 1% crossing; its name wherever the crossing is named by symbol
crossings_plots_axis_names.scope: the axes, keys and prose of the crossings plots; tables and running prose keep the adopted crossing names until the wider naming question on the propositions page is adopted
crossings_plots_axis_names.form: uppercase D50 / D99; on a plot a bound is drawn and labelled as a bound; the scale is named log or logit or left unsaid, never described by its spacing

capC.method_version: capability-C v2026-09-01c (uniform difficulty marginal, full-axis estimator, monotone completion; ci80 bootstrap B=400) + every-model v2026-09-24 (the voters set the axis; every other arm with results is scored on it, the distribution conditioned on the tasks it holds; ci80 with the levels fixed)
capC.name: Capability (uniform)
capC.marginal_plain: population weighted evenly along the failure level (uniform in u on [0, 1]; Voronoi cell mass in u; uncovered easy end credited solved)
capC.distribution: uniform: even weight along the failure level on 0 to 1, Beta(1,1)

frame.population: wave 1+2 (board_top) population: the axis voters on the tasks all of them hold (51 arms): population-relative to these arms; a data point, not the difficulty definition (adopted 2026-09-03)

restriction.label: wave 1+2 (board_top) population: the axis voters on the tasks all of them hold

struck.rule: a position of a course whose register state is 'stopped' is no datapoint on any page or count; out of arms_outside

frame.population_rule: the wave 1+2 axis voters (every arm with at least 90% of the set's tasks scored, the rule of 10 Sep) on the tasks all of them hold; arms below the coverage line are fitted on the axis but carry no C here
frame.hash_note: keep_set_hash is the C population's task rectangle; compare a served wave 1+2 bundle against fit_keep_set_hash (the fit's task set)

every_model.word: the project maintainers' word of 24 Sep 2026: the three capability views available for all the models
every_model.rule: the axis voters (51 arms, the coverage rule of 10 Sep) set the difficulty levels and the uniform weights; every other arm with results on the population's 1256 tasks is a guest scored on the same levels, the uniform distribution conditioned on the tasks it holds: C = credit + mass * sum w (1 - f/n) / sum w over its tasks; a guest holding every task scores as a voter would
every_model.ci80_semantics: guests: the same 80% bootstrap (B=400, fixed seed) with the levels FIXED — the tasks held resampled with replacement and every cell redrawn binomially; a guest does not move the axis
every_model.partial_meaning: partial = coverage (tasks held / population tasks) OR mass_share (the marginal's mass on the tasks held / its mass on all) below the voters' coverage line; the page's partial-models toggle reads it. A partial guest's C is conditioned on the tasks it holds — as a rule the easier end of the axis — and is NOT comparable with a whole model's (the fits critic's measurement, 24 Sep 2026: conditioning a voter on the 430 wave 1 tasks raises its C by +0.16 on average); the flag, not a sentence, carries that

capC.source: analysis/battery/make_u_frame.py (formula: C_m = u_lo + sum_t w_t (1 - f_mt/n_t), Voronoi-in-u weights; uncovered easy end credited solved, hard end failed)
capC.placement_note: z = logit(C): the step-equivalent threshold placement (metrics-report identity)
capC.uncertainty_semantics: ci80_C is an 80% bootstrap interval (10th-90th percentile, B=400, fixed seed) capturing THREE sources jointly per replicate: (1) which tasks the pool holds — tasks resampled with replacement; (2) finite attempts — every kept cell's failure count redrawn binomially at its observed rate; (3) level-position estimation — difficulty levels and cell weights recomputed from the redrawn matrix. The model roster is held FIXED: the scale is population-relative by construction, so roster variation is a scale change, not sampling noise. GUEST ROWS (role guest): the same bootstrap with the LEVELS FIXED — a guest does not move the axis — so their ci80_C carries attempt and task-sampling noise only; each row names its semantics in ci80_semantics.

capC_z.method_version: capability-C v2026-09-14z (difficulty uniform in logit over the axis's task range, Voronoi-in-z weights normalised to one, full-axis estimator, monotone completion; ci80 bootstrap B=400) + every-model v2026-09-24 (the voters set the axis; every other arm with results is scored on it, the distribution conditioned on the tasks it holds; ci80 with the levels fixed)
capC_z.name: Capability (Haldane)
capC_z.marginal_plain: population weighted evenly along the difficulty scale (uniform in logit over the axis's task range; Voronoi cell mass in z, normalised)
capC_z.distribution: Haldane: even weight per logit step over the tasks' range, the improper Beta(0,0) cut at the easiest and hardest task
